'''Rob Reitzen''' is an American mathematician and professional blackjack player. 

==Biography==
Reitzen studied [[mathematics]] and probabilities at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cigaraficionado.com/article/robotic-poker-19354|title=Robotic Poker|first1=Chris |last1=Pratt |first2=James |last2=Gunn |date=2017 |website=[[Cigar Aficionado]]}}</ref> He was initially interested in poker, but shifted his focus to [[blackjack]] after reading Lawrence Revere's ''Playing Blackjack as a Business''.<ref name="auto"/>

In the early 1980s, Reitzen worked with a colleague who later became influential in [[betting on horse racing|horse betting]] technology in [[Hong Kong]].<ref name="auto"/> They used emerging computer technology to develop advanced blackjack techniques, including [[card counting]] systems, [[shuffle track]]ing, and improved methods for memorizing card sequences.<ref name="auto"/>

In the early 1990s, Reitzen co-founded CORE, a company that provided financial and operational support to Native American casinos, including supplying both the bankroll and dealers for blackjack games.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://blackjackhalloffame.com/members/rob-reitzen/|title=Rob Reitzen |website=[[Blackjack Hall of Fame]]}}</ref>

Reitzen also specialized in Texas hold'em poker and developed a mathematical strategy that led to the formation of a successful team under his guidance, which achieved notable success on the Full Tilt Poker platform.<ref name="auto1"/> He later developed another mathematical technique with John Wayne and Darrell Miers that was offered as a service to casinos, as well as to stock and futures markets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/1997/scene/vpage/bruckheimer-teams-on-buy-1117434874/|title=Bruckheimer teams on buy|first1=Anita M. |last1=Busch |first2=Chris|last2=Petrikin|date=April 3, 1997|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

In 1997, Reitzen was featured in ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]'' magazine in an article titled "Fleecing Las Vegas", which described his use of a technique known as "The Hammer" at [[Caesars Palace]].<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/210280809|title=Fleecing Las Vegas |first=Michael |last=Angeli |date=1997 |website=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|id={{ProQuest|210280809}} }}</ref><ref name="auto1"/> The method combined card counting, shuffle tracking, ace location, and card sequence memorization, and reportedly resulted in winnings of $500,000.<ref name="auto2"/>

In 2019, Reitzen was inducted into the [[Blackjack Hall of Fame]].<ref name="auto1"/>

Reitzen is the founder of Random Order Inc and a co-founder of StyleScan, a B2B software specializing in [[artificial intelligence]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://random-order.com/team/|title=About Random Order}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.citybiz.co/article/287884/stylescan-raises-1m/|title=StyleScan Raises $1M|first=Paul|last=Bluemner|date=July 5, 2022}}</ref><ref name="auto"/>
